newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends up, Nov expires sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends up, Nov expires sharply higher.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended up across the board Friday in an active session, with November leading the complex sharply higher on a late wave of short covering before it expired, trade sources said.
November surged 16.7 cents to expire at $2.652 per million British thermal units. December settled 14.8 cents higher at $2.704. Other deferreds ended up by 2.1 to 10.8 cents.

"The winter hasn't even begun, so it's a little early to get too bearish. One (cold) front and we could be off to the races again," said one Midwest trader, adding some late short covering drove the complex to new intraday highs.

But with little extreme weather on the immediate horizon, traders said they expected producers to be on the defensive during bidweek next week. Most Gulf Coast pipeline nomination deadlines are on Tuesday.
Technically, traders pegged December support in the $2.46-47 area, with resistance seen at the recent $2.76 high.

Cash sources said weekend Gulf Coast prices more than a nickel Friday to the $2.40-45 level. Midcon pipes were about five cents lower at about $2.30. New York city gate gas prices continued to be pressured by mild East Coast weather, with quotes ranging from $2.60-2.70, down about 15 cents.
November quotes for New York gas were at NYMEX plus 58 to 64 cents.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip jumped 6.2 cents to $2.269. NYMEX said 81,268 Hub contracts traded, up from Thursday's revised tally of 64,399.
NYMEX November Alberta natgas settled 2.5 cents higher at $1.14, while deferreds closed steady to up two cents. NYMEX said 139 Alberta contracts traded.
NYMEX November Alberta natgas expires Tuesday, October 29.
NYMEX November Permian natgas finished 12 cents higher at $2.44, while deferreds were untraded but up two to eight cents. NYMEX said 72 Permian lots changed hands.
NYMEX November Permian natgas expires Tuesday, October 29.

On the KCBT, November closed up 5.1 cents at $2.47, while deferreds ended 1.5 to five cents higher. The East/West spread widened 11.6 cents to 18.2 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 577 contracts traded, down from Thursday's total of 1,129.
KCBT November natgas expires Monday, October 28.
